proposals: FSSAI should notify a standard of identity for matcha — shade-grown Camellia sinensis leaf, ground, with purity and colour tests — so that a four-fold price rise in a powdered green product does not become an opening for adulterated product sold in India or exported under an Indian origin.

The Tea Board of India should notify grade definitions for Indian matcha, separating ceremonial from culinary and ingredient grade, so that the early pricing decision this post describes is made against a published grade structure rather than lot by lot at auction.

DGFT, with the Tea Board, should create a separate ITC-HS 8-digit line for matcha and powdered green tea, so that Indian production, imports and exports of the category can be tracked in official trade data instead of being lost within aggregated non-black tea.

The Tea Board should publish the results of every matcha and tencha lot sold at Indian auction centres, with volume, price and estate, so that whether the price rises or falls from the first ₹3,000 a kilogram as volumes grow can be followed.

The Tea Research Association at Tocklai, with Tea Board funding, should run and publish multi-year field trials of sinensis cultivars grown under shade in Assam, so that the cultivar constraint this post identifies is addressed with public agronomic data rather than one estate's private decade of work.
